title: Fix _fused_dropout decomposition at keep probability zero
body:
Stack from [ghstack](https://github.com/ezyang/ghstack/tree/0.15.0) (oldest at bottom):
* __->__ #184979

The Python decomposition for aten._fused_dropout computed its scale with
`1.0 / p` as a Python scalar. For the internal fused dropout op, `p` is the
keep probability. CUDA eager computes that division in operator arithmetic, so
`p == 0` produces an infinite scale, an all-zero uint8 mask, and NaN output.
The Python scalar division instead raised ZeroDivisionError during fake tensor
execution, which made torch.compile fail before it could match eager semantics.

Compute the scale as a scalar tensor so the decomposition follows tensor
arithmetic for the edge case. The decomposition previously relied on
`pw_cast_for_opmath`, but that wrapper casts every tensor result back to the
input result dtype, including the mask. Replace it with manual opmath casting
for only the data output so the result keeps the input dtype while the mask
continues to match eager as uint8.

This covers the same issue as stale PR #170547, but preserves the current eager
NaN behavior for keep-probability zero instead of special-casing the result to
zeros.

Fixes #170520
Generated by my agent

Test Plan:
- python test/test_decomp.py -k fused_dropout -v
- lintrunner -a
